block_05_direct_answer.title: Direct answer
block_05_direct_answer.body_html: Project status should be verified through current construction and registration evidence. For ready-property buyers, verify project registration, escrow or payment details where relevant, current status, required approvals and the identity of the contracting developer. Use current official records where available and never treat a sales document alone as proof of regulatory status.

items.question: How can I verify a project's current status?

items.answer: Escrow and permit checks help confirm that an off-plan project follows the required framework. Verify the project status with the relevant authority rather than assuming that marketing activity alone confirms every required registration step.
items.question: How do I check escrow and permits?

items.answer: Live availability can only be confirmed from a current sales or inventory source. Check that the current price, payment plan and any incentive still apply to the exact unit at the time the buyer is ready to proceed.
items.question: How can I verify current availability?

items.answer: A developer check should focus on evidence of delivery, execution and accountability. Treat specific records, documents and project information as stronger evidence than reputation, awards or broad sales assurances.
items.question: How should I assess a developer?

items.answer: Developer track record is best judged through completed projects and delivery behaviour. Repeated delays, unresolved defects or weak execution create doubts about current commitments. Use official project records and completed developments rather than relying only on marketing reputation.
